basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 17.' and it opens 'Vers. 17. Morte morieris. Non de morte corporis dicit, sed de morte animae. Non enim'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 17. Morte morieris. Non de morte corporis dicit, sed de morte animae. Non enim statim ut comedit mortuus est corpore, sed in anima per peccatum. Sed propter mortem animae, id est peccatum, subsecuta est postea suo tempore mors corporis, id est poena peccati.
